punchline: Thaler's dinner guests thanked him for taking away the cashews, which economic theory says they should have resented.
thirty_sec: As a graduate student in the 1970s, Richard Thaler hosted a dinner party and put out cocktails and a bowl of cashews. His guests ate them so fast that he took the bowl away and put it in the pantry. They thanked him. Economic theory says more choices can never hurt, so a roomful of economists were happy about losing one, and he later explained it as willpower: people sometimes want the temptation gone.
